Header:
Date: 2026-03-08
Time: 14:30 PT
Duration: 55m
Attendees: Jordan Li (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Arun Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Crestline), Tommy Nguyen (Crestline), Sasha Alvarez (Crestline)
Links shared: Redwood hosted vs dedicated pricing (link), security whitepaper (link), benchmark template spreadsheet (link)

Summary (auto):
- Customer evaluating tradeoffs between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments for embedding + rerank pipeline.
- Key constraints: VPC-only traffic, SOC2 + KMS requirement, desire to support hybrid search (bm25 + vector rerank), target 2000 QPS at peak for similarity retrieval, unclear on embedding dimensionality tradeoffs (512 vs 1536).
- Agreed next steps: share pricing, run Hosted quick throughput test, send security docs, schedule VPC deep-dive.

Topics: embedding dims, throughput, hybrid rerank, vector DB integration, VPC/KMS, benchmarking plan

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'll do a quick intro then hand over to Maya who'll talk about the perf side.
[00:07] Priya: Yeah hi, thanks. We're excited, we've been evaluating options for our new search stack. Main ask is fast semantic recall and then rerank with our existing bm25 stage.
[00:15] Maya: Great. Quick clarifying q: is your bm25 stage running on Elastic or a custom infra?
[00:20] Sasha: Elastic now, will probably stay that way. We do a top-100 retrieval, then we want vector similarity plus a light cross-encoder for final rerank.
[00:29] Arun: Got it. And target latency for end-to-end should be?
[00:33] Priya: Ideally sub-250ms p50 for customer queries, with p95 under 600ms but we can be flexible if cost explodes.
[00:41] Tommy: Also note we have a strict VPC-only policy for traffic. No internet egress from our search cluster to public APIs.
[00:47] Jordan: That's important — thank you. We'll cover Private options and VPC peering.
[00:52] Maya: On embeddings, two questions folks always ask: dimensionality and storage/throughput tradeoff. Higher dims usually mean better fidelity for some models but higher storage and slower NN search unless you change index config.
[01:05] Sasha: Right, we were leaning toward 1536 dims because our upstream models output 1536 by default. But we worry about throughput at 2k QPS, cost, and index size.
[01:14] Arun: For 2k QPS at 1536d you probably need either a sharded vector DB or a dedicated cluster. Our Dedicated offering can reserve GPU pools and we have optimized kernels for 1536-ish dimensions, but cost is higher.
[01:27] Priya: What about quantizing embeddings or projecting down to 512? Does Redwood recommend that?
[01:33] Maya: We do see good results projecting to 512 for many semantic tasks — often no measurable drop for retrieval if you finetune or use PCA/OPQ. But it depends on your eval set. Also projection reduces index memory and increases throughput.
[01:46] Sasha: Any numbers? We need ballpark for sizing the vector DB and whether to do Dedicated.
[01:50] Maya: From our internal bench, for brute-force ANN on CPU indices, 1536d is ~2.5x memory + slower by ~2x compared to 512d. On GPU-accelerated ANN with HNSW or IVF+PQ the gap narrows because quantization helps. On Redwood Dedicated we co-locate model compute and vector search where useful, which can reduce network hops for rerank.
[02:12] Tommy: If we go Private on-prem, are there constraints for co-locating vector DB? We have strict data residency.
[02:18] Arun: Private supports customer-managed VPC and on-prem deployments. You can bring your DB into the same VPC and we'll run the control plane in your environment, or we can do a hybrid where the control plane is private and compute is in your cloud region.
[02:31] Priya: Security: SOC2, customer-managed KMS for at-rest keys?
[02:34] Jordan: Yes, Private includes KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, HSM options) and audit logs. We'll send the security deck.
[02:42] Sasha: Good. Back to hybrid search — we want to run bm25 first, then vector retrieval, then a cross-encoder. Is that a typical pattern?
[02:48] Maya: Very common. For throughput you can run the initial retrieval in Elastic (fast), do vector similarity on the top-k (e.g., 100) which reduces load, and then run cross-encoder on top 10. That hybrid gives best latency/cost balance.
[02:59] Priya: So if we set top-k to 100, what QPS does vector layer see?
[03:03] Sasha: We're planning to do 2k user queries, times 100 candidate vectors = 200k vector similarity ops per second — but we cache embeddings and many queries overlap so effective QPS at vector layer is lower.
[03:15] Maya: Important detail — Redwood supports prefix/KV caching and automatic batching. If your queries share prefixes we can significantly reduce token cost and also batch embedding/rerank requests. For vector ops we can also batch similarity calls when using a hosted vector index.
[03:28] Tommy: Are you suggesting Redwood hosts the vector DB or we keep Pinecone/Milvus?
[03:33] Arun: We integrate with external DBs (Pinecone, Milvus, Vespa) and we also offer managed vector index in Hosted. It depends on latency, control, and cost. Many customers keep their DB for regulatory reasons.
[03:44] Priya: If we keep our own DB, will Redwood's dedicated instances still be able to call into it over VPC?
[03:50] Jordan: Yes, with VPC peering or private endpoint. We'll need your network team to open specific ports; Tommy, you'd share the firewall policy.
[03:57] Tommy: Yup that's in the action items.
[04:00] Sasha: For the throughput test, what's the minimal configuration to simulate our stack?
[04:05] Maya: We'll do a Hosted run first: ingest your sample embeddings (both 512 and 1536 variants) into a test index, then replay your query set at target QPS. We'll measure p50/p95, CPU/GPU utilization, and index memory. That should give signals on whether to choose 512 or 1536 and whether Dedicated is warranted.
[04:21] Priya: How long does the Hosted run take?
[04:24] Maya: We can spin up a 1-hour run, results in 24 hours. The run itself is usually 30-90 min for the load stage.
[04:31] Sasha: Will the test include cross-encoder rerank latency?
[04:35] Arun: We can simulate cross-encoder either with a small BERT-like model on-hosted or point at your cross-encoder running in your infra through the VPC. But best to test both.
[04:45] Priya: Anything else about embeddings themselves — do you recommend storing float32 or quantized?
[04:50] Maya: For hosted vector indices we often store compressed PQ/OPQ representations which are integers; for in-house Milvus some teams store FP16 to balance precision and memory. We can show the recommended configs in the benchmark template.
[04:59] Jordan: A few real-world tradeoffs: if you need strict reproducibility and no lossy quantization we recommend FP16 or FP32. If cost and storage dominate, PQ is the way and 512 dims is usually enough.
[05:12] Sasha: Ok one more — model versioning and rollouts. We can't have surprise regressions in search quality.
[05:17] Maya: Redwood has model pinning and rollout policies. You can set canary percentage, automatic fallback to a baseline if quality drops (we can tie it to prompt-based evals), and token-level cost tracing so you know the economics per call.
[05:31] Priya: That sounds good.
[05:33] Jordan: Quick recap: we'll share pricing, security docs, and run a Hosted throughput test using your sample data, both 512 and 1536 embeddings. We'll schedule a VPC/KMS deep-dive. Any final Qs?
[05:44] Priya: No, that's it. Thanks team.
[05:46] Jordan: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the links and the test plan.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcript imperfections: occasional misattribution (Speaker labels generic in parts), small ASR errors (OPQ sometimes transcribed as O-P-Q, KMS noted as K-M-S), and intermittent punctuation drops.
